label: KitCommerce vs Dukaan
summary: A quick-start Indian store builder with a free plan and a service fee on every sale — against an open-source platform with no fee when you run it yourself, and more work up front.
title: KitCommerce vs Dukaan: Plans, Service Fee and Code Access
description: Dukaan vs GoCommerce and Svelte Commerce: plans, Dukaan’s service fee on sales by plan, payments and shipping — and where Dukaan wins.
ogDescription: Dukaan starts free and takes a service fee as you sell. GoCommerce takes nothing per sale when you run it yourself, and asks for a developer. Sourced.
h1: Dukaan is free to start and charges as you sell. GoCommerce run yourself is the other way round.
lede: Dukaan gets a store online from the web or its Android and iOS apps, with a free plan — then takes a service fee of 0.99% to 4.99% of sales, by plan, on top of the payment gateway’s charge. Run GoCommerce and Svelte Commerce yourself and they take nothing per sale, but ask for a server and a developer before the first one. A store hosted on kitcommerce.store pays {hostedFee} of each successful sale.

glanceLede: Dukaan’s side is taken from its pricing page — plan cards, comparison table and FAQ — linked at the foot of this page. Ours is what GoCommerce and Svelte Commerce do today.
rows: What it is
A hosted store builder, run from the web or Dukaan’s Android and iOS apps on every plan.
An open-source platform in two MIT packages: GoCommerce for the backend and a web admin, Svelte Commerce for the storefront. Run it yourself, or start a store hosted on kitcommerce.store.
Plans
Free, Starter, Growth and Infinity, the paid ones billed monthly or yearly.
None. Run it yourself and the software costs nothing; a store hosted on kitcommerce.store pays {hostedFee} of each successful sale.
Service fee on sales
4.99% on Free, 3.99% on Starter, 1.99% on Growth and 0.99% on Infinity — capped per order, not charged on manual orders, and on top of gateway charges.
None when you run it yourself. A store hosted on kitcommerce.store pays {hostedFee} of each successful sale.
Payment gateways
Cashfree, Razorpay, PayPal and Stripe.
Eleven payment modules, Cashfree, Razorpay and Stripe among them; cash on delivery is the core’s default method.
Shipping
Dukaan Delivery built in; Shiprocket and Shippo, or your own Blue Dart, Delhivery, DTDC or Xpressbees account.
Shiprocket, Delhivery and NimbusPost modules book shipments; India Post consignments are recorded; Shippo, ShipStation and others for parcels abroad.
Stores and staff
1 store on Free and Starter, 3 on Growth, 10 on Infinity; 1, 2, 5 and 20 staff accounts.
Channels for several storefronts and roles for staff, with no count set by a plan.
Customising
Themes from Dukaan’s marketplace, and a code editor for fonts, colours and theme sections.
The source — storefront, checkout and backend.
Moving in
Imports catalogues from Shopify, WooCommerce, Gumroad or a CSV file, and can keep your old URL structure.
Imports a whole Shopify catalogue, safely re-runnable; from anything else, a script against the documented API.
Running it from a phone
Dukaan’s Android and iOS apps, on every plan.
No app. The admin is a web app compiled into the GoCommerce binary.
Hosting
Dukaan’s.
Yours when you run it — a single Go binary beside a PostgreSQL database, on any server you choose. Or hosted on kitcommerce.store, for {hostedFee} of each successful sale.
Who it is for
Dukaan says it is tailored to online businesses that depend on repeat purchases.
Stores with a developer, and developers building stores for others.

cost.note: From Dukaan’s plan table. Dukaan’s fee is capped per order and not charged on manual orders; the paid plans add a monthly or yearly price on top. The gateway’s own charge is paid on every set-up and left out; Razorpay lists 2% + GST. Dukaan’s FAQ, on the same page, quotes different rates for differently named plans; we have used the plan table.

themWhen: You want to start selling today on a free plan, from your phone, and pay only once sales come in.
Your sales are small, so a few per cent of them costs less than paying someone to run a server.
You want delivery, payments and the store in one place, with no code at all.
You are testing a product idea and may not need a store in six months.
usWhen: Your sales have grown to where Dukaan’s fee is a real line, and a server and a developer would cost less.
You want to change the checkout and the order flow, not only the theme.
You want your store’s data in a database you control, under software with an MIT licence.
You have, or can hire, a developer — the one cost running GoCommerce yourself cannot remove.
takeOnExtra: No phone app to run the store from — the admin is a web app.
No built-in delivery service: you bring your own Shiprocket, Delhivery or NimbusPost account.

faq.q: Does Dukaan charge a fee on sales?
faq.a: Yes. Dukaan’s plan table lists a service fee of 4.99% on Free, 3.99% on Starter, 1.99% on Growth and 0.99% on Infinity, capped per order and not charged on manual orders. Its FAQ adds that the fee is exclusive of payment gateway charges. GoCommerce charges no fee on sales when you run it yourself; a store hosted on kitcommerce.store pays {hostedFee} of each successful sale.
Free, Starter, Growth and Infinity. The paid plans are billed monthly or yearly, and each step up lowers the service fee; the higher plans also allow more stores and staff accounts.

faq.q: Which payment gateways work on each?
faq.a: Dukaan lists Cashfree, Razorpay, PayPal and Stripe. GoCommerce has eleven payment modules, Cashfree, Razorpay and Stripe among them, and cash on delivery in the core; PayPal is not among its modules.

faq.q: Can I move from Dukaan to GoCommerce?
faq.a: There is no Dukaan importer, so moving means a script against GoCommerce’s documented API. The one catalogue importer GoCommerce has is for Shopify.

faq.q: Can Svelte Commerce be the storefront for a Dukaan store?
faq.a: No. Dukaan is not among the 26 backends Svelte Commerce connects to. Svelte Commerce reaches GoCommerce through an early connector, 0.1.0, covering catalogue, cart, checkout and order lookup; customer accounts and search are not covered yet.
